raw: 30.7 Stasi: East German Pervasive Domestic Intelligence
teaching_note: Stasi history concerns dictatorship, repression and affected persons, not merely efficient source protection; the Federal Archives describes historical reappraisal and individuals' access to records about themselves (https://www.bundesarchiv.de/en/stasi-records-archive/). Completed offline case: S1 is a synthetic security-service file asserting a person's disloyalty, S2 an independent dated publication contradicting its factual allegation, S3 a later archive release with redactions, and S4 an affected-person correction. The filled result is 'the institution recorded an allegation' (S1), not 'the allegation is true'; S2/S4 challenge it, while S3 establishes later access but not missing content. Withheld S5 reveals S1 copied an earlier unverified file, so collapse the apparent corroboration and retract the adverse claim; stop person-level inference and retain the correction (see [@sec:analytic-workflow]). This fictional case illustrates critical reading of coercive archives, not any real person's history or a measured account of all Stasi practice.
title: Stasi: East German repression and archival accountability
